c.tagline: The Windy City of soaring architecture, deep-dish, blues, and Lake Michigan shoreline.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around $3.25 plus per-mile and per-minute charges; a small citywide surcharge applies. App-based Uber and Lyft are widely used and often cheaper.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance; 311 is the city's non-emergency line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The South and West Sides (Englewood, Garfield Park) have high crime — avoid. The Loop and Mag Mile are safe.

hood_desc: Chicago's central business and cultural core, home to Millennium Park and 'the Bean', the Art Institute, Willis Tower, and the Chicago Theatre; the classic first-timer base, ringed by the elevated 'L' tracks and steps from the riverwalk and lakefront.
A lively district just north of the river packed with art galleries, rooftop bars, steakhouses, and nightclubs; the go-to area for dining and nightlife within walking distance of downtown.
A trendy, artsy Northwest Side neighborhood of indie boutiques, record shops, vintage stores, murals, and buzzy bars and cafes; popular with a young, creative crowd.
A leafy, affluent lakefront neighborhood wrapped around its namesake park and free zoo, with Victorian rowhouses, the DePaul campus, boutiques, and family-friendly streets.
A historic, intellectual South Side enclave centered on the University of Chicago, with the Museum of Science and Industry, the Obama Presidential Center, leafy streets, and lakefront parks.
lodging: Hotel Lincoln, a JdV by Hyatt
The Study at the University of Chicago

water.note: Tap water from Lake Michigan is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Pay with a Ventra card or tap a contactless bank card or phone at 'L' turnstiles and bus readers. A single 'L' ride is $2.50 and buses are $2.25; a 1-day unlimited pass is $5. Ventra cards cost $5, which converts to transit value.
transit.hours: The Red and Blue Lines run 24 hours a day; other 'L' lines run roughly 4am to 1am. Buses vary, with several 24-hour routes.

tip.r: ~18-20% at restaurants; $1-2 per drink at bars and ~15% for taxi rides.

food.name: Deep-dish pizza
food.desc: A buttery high-walled crust layered with mozzarella, sausage and chunky tomato on top. It takes 45 minutes to bake, so order when you sit down.

places.name: Pequod's Pizza
places.note: Caramelized burnt-cheese crust ring; routinely ranked the country's best pan pizza.

places.name: Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
places.note: The buttercrust benchmark since 1971; get The Malnati Chicago Classic with sausage patty.

places.name: Milly's Pizza in the Pan
places.note: Cult pre-order pan pizza named among the world's best; plan ahead, it sells out.

food.name: Italian beef
food.desc: Thin-sliced slow-roasted beef on French bread, topped with sweet peppers or spicy giardiniera and dunked in its own gravy. Order it dipped, eat standing.

places.name: Al's No. 1 Italian Beef
places.note: Serving since 1938 and half of the city's great beef rivalry; hot giardiniera is essential.

places.name: Johnnie's Beef
places.note: Cash-only stand locals drive out for; pair the beef with a tart Italian lemonade.

places.name: Portillo's
places.note: The easy in-town option; get the combo with a char-grilled sausage and a chocolate cake shake.

food.name: Chicago-style hot dog
food.desc: All-beef frank in a poppy seed bun dragged through the garden: mustard, neon relish, onion, tomato, pickle spear, sport peppers, celery salt. No ketchup.

places.name: Gene and Jude's
places.note: Depression-style dog with fresh-cut fries piled on top; no seats, no ketchup, no exceptions.

places.name: Superdawg Drive-In
places.note: 1948 drive-in with carhop service, crinkle fries and a pickled green tomato in the box.

places.name: The Wieners Circle
places.note: Char dogs and legendary late-night staff heckling; a Chicago experience as much as a meal.

food.name: Jibarito
food.desc: Invented in Chicago's Puerto Rican community: steak, garlic mayo, cheese, lettuce and tomato pressed between two flattened fried green plantains.

places.name: Jibaritos Y Mas
places.note: Eleven versions including churrasco, octopus and a Cubano jibarito; garlicky fried plantain.

places.name: Omarcito's Latin Cafe
places.note: Named the city's best jibarito in a 2026 Axios taste test.

places.name: Papa's Cache Sabroso
places.note: Longtime Paseo Boricua staple; also famous for its garlic rotisserie chicken.

food.name: Maxwell Street Polish
food.desc: Grilled Polish sausage buried in mounds of caramelized onions with yellow mustard and sport peppers, a South Side street-food legacy of Maxwell Street market.

places.name: Jim's Original
places.note: The original stand, open 24 hours since 1939; onions have been on the griddle all day.

places.name: Express Grill
places.note: The rival stand right next door, also 24 hours; pick a side and commit.

food.name: Malort
food.desc: Jeppson's Malort, a punishing wormwood liqueur locals dare visitors to try. Order a Chicago Handshake: a shot of Malort with a can of Old Style.

places.name: CH Distillery
places.note: Now produces Jeppson's Malort in the city; the cocktail bar makes it almost pleasant.

places.name: Old Town Ale House
places.note: Classic dive across from Second City with painted regulars and a straight-faced Handshake.

food.name: Chicago craft beer
food.desc: A deep brewery scene stretching from Goose Island, which helped launch American craft, to a wall of neighborhood taprooms pouring lagers and barrel-aged stouts.

places.name: Goose Island Beer Company
places.note: Fulton Street taproom; the Bourbon County stout program started here.

places.name: Half Acre Beer Company
places.note: Beloved local brewery; Daisy Cutter pale ale is a Chicago fridge staple.

places.name: Revolution Brewing
places.note: Illinois' largest independent brewery, with a big taproom and Anti-Hero IPA on tap.

landmarks: Cloud Gate ("The Bean")
The mirror-polished steel sculpture in Millennium Park reflects the skyline in endlessly photogenic curves.
Willis Tower Skydeck
One of the tallest buildings in the Western Hemisphere, its glass Ledge balconies give a dizzying view straight down over the city.
Navy Pier
A lakefront pier with a giant Centennial Wheel that frames striking sunset shots over Lake Michigan.
Art Institute of Chicago
A world-class museum whose iconic bronze lion statues flank a grand Michigan Avenue entrance.
Millennium Park
A downtown green space combining public art, the Jay Pritzker Pavilion band shell, and skyline backdrops.
Chicago Riverwalk
A scenic promenade along the Chicago River offering unique low-angle views of the city's famous architecture.
Chicago Theatre
The historic marquee with its giant vertical "CHICAGO" sign is one of the most recognizable nighttime shots in the city.
Chicago Water Tower
A castle-like limestone landmark that famously survived the Great Chicago Fire, standing out amid modern Michigan Avenue high-rises.
Wrigley Field
The ivy-covered outfield walls and classic red marquee make this century-old ballpark a beloved photo subject.
Museum of Science and Industry
A grand Beaux-Arts building, the last surviving structure from the 1893 World's Fair, set on the lakefront.

train.note: Chicago Union Station is the hub of the entire US long-distance network: eight long-distance routes radiate from it, including the California Zephyr to San Francisco, the Empire Builder to Seattle and Portland, the Southwest Chief to Los Angeles, the City of New Orleans, the Lake Shore Limited to New York and Boston, the Texas Eagle, the Cardinal and the Floridian, plus eight corridor services such as the Hiawatha to Milwaukee and Lincoln Service to St Louis. Six Metra commuter lines also terminate there. No train crosses into Canada from Chicago - the nearest cross-border services are Amtrak's Maple Leaf and Adirondack out of New York. Sleeper space on the western trains opens 11 months ahead and the cheapest buckets go quickly.

intl.to: Monterrey, San Luis Potosi, Guadalajara, Morelia & central Mexico

bus.note: Tornado Bus Company runs Chicago's cross-border coaches from its own terminal, taking well over 30 hours to central Mexico with a passport check and FMM tourist card at the border. Domestic services use the Greyhound terminal at 630 West Harrison Street just southwest of the Loop, while FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) mostly load curbside near Union Station. Typical times are about 90 minutes to Milwaukee, four hours to Indianapolis, five to St Louis and five to Detroit. Everything is cheapest booked online a week or two ahead.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled intercity ferry from Chicago itself. Shoreline Sightseeing and the Chicago Water Taxi run seasonal commuter and sightseeing boats on the Chicago River and along the lakefront between Navy Pier, the Loop and Museum Campus, but they are local transport. The nearest true car ferry across Lake Michigan is the Lake Express from Milwaukee to Muskegon, about 90 miles north, or the SS Badger from Manitowoc to Ludington.

half.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
half.blurb: Towering sand dunes and beaches along Lake Michigan's southern shore, with hiking trails through dune-and-swale ecosystems.

half.name: Starved Rock State Park
half.blurb: Sandstone canyons, waterfalls and river bluffs along the Illinois River, laced with popular hiking trails.

half.name: Milwaukee
half.blurb: A lakefront Wisconsin city known for its art museum's wing-like addition, breweries and revitalized riverside districts.

full.name: Galena
full.blurb: A preserved 19th-century river town of brick storefronts and Civil War-era mansions in the hills of northwest Illinois.
